- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >80), model often overreacts with continued upward bias; cap forecast at +5–10% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral.
- If sentiment is consistently negative or mixed (≤ 0.33), model underestimates; add 2–5% to forecast to account for mean reversion or hidden support.
- Model frequently overpredicts in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile; apply smoothing or lag correction for short-term forecasts.
- For 10+ day horizons, model tends to underestimate unless sentiment is strongly bullish; increase forecast by 3–7% if sentiment > 0.67 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; trigger a “sentiment pivot” correction: add 1–3% to forecast at pivot point.
- Avoid forecasting above 85% of recent 30-day high unless sentiment is >0.80 and sustained; cap at 85–90% to prevent overcorrection.
